cases.name: Linda Mercurio
cases.about: Mercurio frequently sought help for her son, several friends said. She asked Poehlmann to write a letter to a judge after one of his assault convictions, and she took him to a Zen center for meditational healing. It fit with who she was. “Linda was a calm, lovely human being,” said Cynthia Frank, who directs the women’s choir. “She was a good mother, and we’re all shocked and appalled at what happened.” Struggling to help her son didn’t mean Mercurio didn’t live a full life, though. She ran an import business, traveled frequently, created artwork in her home, and frequently attended gatherings at the Zen center with her husband, Robert Pinkham, who died in 2021. Her skills as a singer dovetailed nicely with her daughter’s keyboard expertise, Frank said, and in 2006 they performed with the women’s choir at Carnegie Hall in New York and at a church at 9/11’s ground zero.
